I'd downloaded some silly video filter app a while back.
It was mostly for messing around with my niece over video calls.
I completely forgot it was still connected to my laptop's camera settings.
A big client meeting got moved up last minute.
I barely had time to grab my laptop, find a decent looking wall behind me, and join the call.
I felt pretty proud of myself for making it on time at all.
About two minutes in, my manager paused mid-sentence.
She asked, kind of carefully, whether I meant to look like that on camera.
Honestly, that confused me for a second, because I had no idea what she meant.
I asked her what she was talking about.
I felt pretty confused.
She just said, slowly, that maybe I should check my own video preview before continuing.
I looked down at the little video preview, and there I was.
A fully animated cartoon cat, complete with whiskers, ears, and blinking cartoon eyes.
It was nodding along seriously to a conversation about quarterly numbers.
I tried clicking around frantically, looking for the button to turn it off.
But every click seemed to make things worse.
At one point I even gave myself little cat paws that moved whenever I talked with my hands.
The whole meeting had gone completely silent, except for one guy who was clearly trying very hard not to laugh.
His shoulders shook slightly, and he kept staring down at his own screen instead of mine.
Someone else typed into the chat and asked if this was a new company mascot we hadn't been told about yet.
Honestly, that didn't help my situation at all.
Now people were actively commenting on it instead of politely ignoring it.
I finally just said, out loud, "I'm not a cat, I promise." Honestly, that made the entire thing so much funnier.
It somehow broke the tension enough that people started actually laughing instead of just awkwardly holding it in.
I ended up just turning my camera off entirely for the rest of the meeting.
I blamed "technical issues" and frantically googled how to disable the filter app in the background.
It took me almost ten minutes of searching before I finally found the tiny toggle buried three menus deep.
Now I check my camera settings before every single call, cat filter or not.
My manager still brings it up sometimes, usually asking if the cat has any thoughts on the agenda.
Somebody on the team even made a small graphic of the cartoon cat and quietly set it as the meeting room's default background image.
I only found out weeks later, during a completely unrelated call.
